req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE but NOT HEAD or OPTIONS explicitly (Flask handles HEAD automatically for GET routes; OPTIONS may or may not be supported). Tests cover: (1) positive EP for each explicitly listed verb returning the exact requested status code, (2) boundary BVA for status codes at edges of 2xx range (200, 299), (3) negative NEG for invalid/non-numeric status codes returning 400, (4) DT for all verbs in the route decorator, (5) BVA for boundary codes 199/200/201 and 299/300/301 to catch off-by-one mutations in status_code helper, (6) NEG for 5xx server error codes, (7) STC for weighted/comma-separated codes path. Each test uses exact status code assertions to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_code
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each to /status/200 and /status/404
expected: Each verb returns exactly the requested status code
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 -> all verbs -> exact status code returned
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_code():
    methods = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('PATCH', client.patch),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
    ]
    for verb, fn in methods:
        r = fn('/status/200')
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"{verb} /status/200 got {r.status_code}"
        r = fn('/status/404')
        assert r.status_code == 404, f"{verb} /status/404 got {r.status_code}"

test_all_verbs_return_correct_status_code()

tests.name: test_each_verb_returns_its_own_exact_code
expected: Each verb returns exactly 202 or 503 as requested
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 -> EP all verbs with distinct codes -> exact match
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_each_verb_returns_its_own_exact_code():
    pairs = [
        (client.get, 202),
        (client.post, 503),
        (client.put, 202),
        (client.patch, 503),
        (client.delete, 202),
    ]
    for fn, code in pairs:
        r = fn(f'/status/{code}')
        assert r.status_code == code, f"Expected {code}, got {r.status_code}"

test_each_verb_returns_its_own_exact_code()
